isolation.notes: Used isolated temp directory for all CLI commands. No real browser cookies or X/Twitter API access available.

results.title: Full pipeline — Helium sync → search → classify
results.evidence:
Tested CLI pipeline with seeded data in isolated temp directory:
1. `ft sync --browser helium --help` — exits 0, shows --browser flag accepting the helium option
2. Created bookmarks.jsonl with 3 sample bookmarks (TypeScript, security, launch categories)
3. `ft index` — built SQLite FTS5 index: 'Indexed 3 bookmarks (3 new)'
4. `ft search 'TypeScript'` — found the TypeScript bookmark correctly
5. `ft classify --regex` — classified 2/3 bookmarks (security + launch categories)
6. `ft list` — showed all 3 bookmarks with classification categories
Data flow verified: JSONL → SQLite FTS5 index → search queries → classification categories.

frictions.description: Cannot perform a real sync with Helium browser cookies (no browser installed in CI). Verified command registration and data flow with seeded data instead.
frictions.resolution: Used seeded JSONL data to verify the downstream pipeline (index, search, classify, list). Sync command acceptance verified separately.

results.title: Sync → Wiki → Ask knowledge base roundtrip
results.evidence:
Tested CLI knowledge base pipeline with seeded data in isolated temp directory:
1. Seeded 3 bookmarks in bookmarks.jsonl
2. `ft index` — built index from JSONL
3. `ft md` — 'Exported 3/3 bookmarks', created md/bookmarks/ directory with 3 markdown files
4. `ft wiki` — created wiki structure (categories/, concepts/, domains/, entities/ directories plus index.md, log.md, md-state.json)
5. `ft ask --help` — exits 0, shows question argument and --save/--json options
Data flow verified: bookmarks.jsonl → md export → wiki structure. Ask command is available but requires LLM engine.

frictions.description: Cannot test ft ask end-to-end without LLM engine (Claude/Codex). Verified command registration and help output.
frictions.resolution: Verified ask command is available and correctly registered. Full LLM Q&A would require API credentials.
